**Publish gate report: landing hero**

**Going out:** Landing page hero, Pebblebrook Tea Co. website.

**Claims check**
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website" | On the policy list (review export, Oct 2026). Exact wording, OK. |
| "The finest organic loose leaf" | "Finest" is a banned superlative. "Organic" is only allowed as "Certified organic by the Soil Association". Remove "finest"; use the approved wording. |
| "eco-friendly bags" | Banned general green claim. The provable version is "plastic-free and home compostable". |
| "packed by hand in Bristol" | On the policy list. OK (policy says "every tin", so "Every tin is packed by hand in Bristol" is the exact claim; "packed by hand" about the tea and bags generally goes slightly beyond it). |

**Regulated claims:** The environmental claim ("eco-friendly") is the risky line. Replace it with the certified specifics.

**House style:** No banned words. The voice is a bit stiff and list-like, not very warm or unhurried. The two sentences are fine but could be plainer.

**Disclosure:** Own-site copy, no partnership, affiliate or AI content. No label needed.

**Fixed (suggested rewrite):**
> Rated 4.8 out of 5 from over 1,200 reviews on our website. Certified organic by the Soil Association, with plastic-free, home compostable tea bags. Every tin is packed by hand in Bristol.

**Needs a decision:**
- Confirm the rewrite is acceptable. It drops "finest" and "eco-friendly" and uses only the policy's exact claim wording.
- "Loose leaf" was removed from the organic phrase; if you want it, "Certified organic loose leaf tea" would need the product team to confirm that all loose leaf is covered by the certificate.

**Approver:** Sam (marketing lead). Nothing should go live until Sam says yes to the final text. I have not recorded any approval.

**Verdict:** Do not publish the draft as written.
